neighbours.label: the tokens ' baker', 'aper' (in dr-aper, dr-aper-ies) and 'apper' (in tr-apper): tradesman-word pieces
fire: In those days the town had one draper, who also sold buttons and thread.
Every morning the baker left warm rolls outside our door.
An old trapper showed us where the beavers had dammed the creek.
She chose thick velvet draperies for the tall windows of the hall.
My uncle worked as a baker in Lyon for thirty years.
He was apprenticed to a linen draper in the high street at fourteen.
The street is lined with small bakeries and coffee shops.
A French trapper built the first cabin beside the lake.
quiet: In those days the town had one tailor, who also sold buttons and thread.
Every morning the milkman left cold bottles outside our door.
An old hunter showed us where the beavers had dammed the creek.
She chose thick velvet curtains for the tall windows of the hall.
My uncle worked as a butcher in Lyon for thirty years.
He was apprenticed to a wool weaver in the high street at fourteen.
The street is lined with small newspaper stands and coffee shops.
A French rapper filmed his first video beside the lake.

notes: Layer 3, card: 'aper' x7, ' baker' x7, 'apper' x3, 'akers' x3. Probes: draper 0.88, draperies 0.91, baker 0.52, trapper 0.42; butcher 0.06, wrapper 0.01, rapper 0.03, newspaper 0.01, Quakers / shoemakers 0.01. A list of tokens, not a meaning: other trades do not fire, and the - pole is another set of -er pieces ('izer', 'iders', 'iter').
